title: release.yml feeds vars.REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS into arithmetic unvalidated in its post-publish visibility wait
description:
Found by the LCLI-629 reviewer (2026-09-28): a fourth reader of the registry window. .github/workflows/release.yml sets REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS from the repository variable (vars.REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS, falling back to 1800) at line 1299 and uses it at line 1333 as deadline=$(( started + REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS )), with no check. LCLI-629 made scripts/publish-release.sh refuse anything outside ^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,8})$, the grammar readme-readback.sh and promote-latest.mjs (REGISTRY_WINDOW) already share. release.yml was deliberately left out of that branch.

NOT MEASURED. What follows is the inference of the reviewer, not a measurement. With abc the window would be 0 seconds, so a lagging package would get a warning annotation and a green step, without its dist.shasum check. With 30m the step would fail and put a red X on a good release. The step runs after the publish, so it gates no publish either way. The runner is ubuntu-latest with its own shell version, not the macOS 3.2 shell LCLI-629 measured, so those measurements do not transfer and have to be re-taken.

As a release.yml change it needs its own reviewer pass before it lands (repository rule: anything touching release.yml or scripts/ gets a reviewer).

acceptanceCriteria.text: The behaviour of the release.yml visibility wait on a malformed vars.REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS (at least abc, 30m, 08 and empty) is measured on the runner shell, and recorded here before any fix
The step refuses a value outside the REGISTRY_WINDOW grammar before it waits, naming the variable and showing the value escaped, and a test pins that its pattern equals REGISTRY_WINDOW.source
bun test and bun run lint:shell exit 0; a reviewer pass covers the release.yml change

plan: 1. Measure first (AC1): extract the release.yml visibility-wait step and run its actual lines with REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS set to abc, 30m, 08 and empty in an ubuntu:24.04 container bash via docker, recording bash --version. Record the table on this task before any fix.

2. Fix (AC2): inside the step, before the wait, refuse any value outside the REGISTRY_WINDOW grammar shared with publish-release.sh, readme-readback.sh and promote-latest.mjs, naming REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS and printing the value escaped, in the publish-release.sh refusal style.

3. Test: new test/lcli630-release-window-guard.test.ts pins that the release.yml pattern equals the imported REGISTRY_WINDOW.source, and runs the extracted step to prove a malformed value is refused and a valid one accepted.

4. Gates: bun test, bun run lint, bun run lint:shell, actionlint on release.yml, bun run lore check from source. Open a PR to dev titled fix(LCLI-630), note measurement, gates and PR here. Reviewer pass (AC3) is the dispatcher's; do not complete.
implementationNotes:
AC1 MEASUREMENT, taken 2026-09-28 before any change to release.yml (branch fix/LCLI-630-release-window-guard at d805dc69, release.yml identical to origin/dev 87207895).

OBJECT MEASURED: the run block of the publish job's step "Verify the registry serves what was published (LCLI-460)", extracted verbatim from release.yml with js-yaml (sha256 99f6c18a7bf70712d18913ab36801c906e6330343710e9c8308924a25d3cdd7e), written to a file and run as `bash -e <file>`. That is GitHub's documented invocation for a Linux step with no `shell:` key; the step has none, and neither the publish job nor the workflow has a `defaults:` block, so it is NOT `shell: bash` (which adds --noprofile --norc -o pipefail). Shell: ubuntu:24.04 Docker container, GNU bash 5.2.21(1)-release, run twice: aarch64 (native, Apple silicon) and x86_64 (--platform linux/amd64 under emulation). ubuntu-latest is ubuntu-24.04 with bash 5.2.21, but this is NOT a GitHub runner. Only two things were stubbed: `node` (ubuntu:24.04 ships none; it only reads name@version out of package.json) and `npm` (lag = every `npm view` exits 1; visible = version and a matching dist.shasum). One staged tarball. Each run bounded by `timeout 45`, so exit 124 means it was still running at 45s.

RESULTS (every exit code and behaviour identical on both architectures; times are aarch64):
| value | npm | exit | time | what happened |
| abc | lag | 0 | 0s | window silently 0 (abc read as an unset variable name): no wait, ::warning:: "after abcs", green; the lagging package gets no content check |
| 30m | lag | 124 | >45s | "30m: value too great for base" at the deadline line; bash -e does NOT stop (an arithmetic expansion error in a script file aborts that line only), deadline stays EMPTY, both [ -ge ]/[ -gt ] tests print "integer expression expected" and never break, so it NEVER EXITS: sleeps 5,10,20,40,60,60... forever, printing a negative "s of the shared window left". Bounded only by the job timeout; the publish job sets none (GitHub default 360 min, not measured here) |
| 08 | lag | 124 | >45s | same as 30m: "08: value too great for base", never exits |
| (empty) | lag | 0 | 0s | same as abc: window 0, warning "after s", green |
| abc | visible | 0 | 0s | visible, content check matches, green |
| 30m | visible | 0 | 0s | arithmetic error printed, then pending empties before the deadline test is reached, content check matches, GREEN with an error line in the log |
| 08 | visible | 0 | 0s | same as 30m visible |
| (empty) | visible | 0 | 0s | green, content matches |
Controls: 0/lag exit 0 at 0s; 7/lag exit 0 after 7s (waited 5+2); 1800/visible exit 0. Extra shapes outside the grammar, all accepted today: 0x10/lag waited 16s (hex), -5/lag window 0, " 3"/lag waited 3s.

WHAT THIS CORRECTS in the filing inference: "30m would fail the step and put a red X on a good release" is FALSE on bash 5.2. 30m and 08 are green when everything is already visible, and hang the job (not fail it) when anything lags. abc and empty behave as inferred (window 0, warning, green, no content check for the laggard). Empty is reachable only if the env line changes: `vars.X || 1800` maps an unset or empty variable to 1800.

METHOD NOTE: running only the deadline line under `bash -e -c "...; deadline=...; ..."` exits 1 on 30m/08, because in -c the whole string is one input line and the error discards the rest of it. That is a different object from the step and gave the wrong answer; only the file form reproduces what the runner does.

ONE MORE SHAPE, same fixture and invocation, both architectures: REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS='x[$(touch /tmp/w/PWNED)]' with a lagging registry exits 0 and the file EXISTS afterwards. $(( started + REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS )) evaluates the value as an arithmetic expression, and an array subscript's command substitution runs. So today the repository (or release-environment) variable is code that runs in the publish job, the one job holding id-token: write. Who can set that variable was not measured.

Harness scripts and raw output: scratchpad only (harness.sh, harness2.sh, before.txt, before-amd64.txt); nothing committed.

FIX AND GATES, opum-ai/lore-cli#358 (branch fix/LCLI-630-release-window-guard, fix commit b1dbf428).

The step now checks window_re, the literal ^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,8})$, first, before spec_of_tgz, any npm view, the deadline and any sleep. A value outside it prints one ::error:: line that names REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS, shows the value through printf %q with every % written %25, and says that nothing was verified and not to unpublish. It then exits 2.

AFTER-FIX MEASUREMENT, same object as the AC1 note (ubuntu:24.04 container, bash 5.2.21 aarch64, the fixed block extracted verbatim and run as bash -e <file>):
- abc, 30m, 08 and empty, against both a lagging and a visible registry: exit 2 at 0s, with the refusal line and no registry read.
- 0x10, -5 and " 3" (leading space): exit 2.
- The subscript value: exit 2, and its file was NOT created.
- Controls 0/lag, 7/lag and 1800/visible: exit 0, same behaviour as before.

TEST: test/lcli630-release-window-guard.test.ts, 18 tests.
- The step's window_re literal equals the imported REGISTRY_WINDOW.source.
- The check comes before npm view, the deadline and sleep.
- The step has no shell: key and no defaults: block, and keeps its env expression.
- The real block, run as bash -e <file> against a stub npm, refuses 11 malformed values: exit 2, one line, the escaped value, no npm call. It accepts 0, 2, 1800 and 999999999.

MUTATION CHECK. Each subset was predicted from the test file before the run, and each result matched:
- guard removed: 13 of 18 red
- looser ^[0-9]+$: 3 red
- %25 escape dropped: 1 red
- %q dropped: 3 red
A first looser-grammar mutant broke the YAML (JS replace expanded $') and turned all 18 red. That red was not localised, so it was discarded and re-run with a function replacer.

GATES (local macOS; bun 1.3.14, lore 0.11.0 from source, quest 0.11.0, shellcheck 0.11.0, actionlint 1.7.12):
- bun test: exit 0. 4327 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail across 4328 tests in 121 files.
- bun run lint: exit 0. Its 4 warnings and 1 info are all in untouched files.
- bun run lint:shell: exit 0.
- actionlint release.yml: exit 0. Positive control: a copy with [ -n $X ] injected into this step exits 1 with SC2070.
- bun run lore check: exit 0 (82 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings).
One flake was found and fixed before commit: the "2s of the shared window left" assertion depended on the second boundary and now accepts 1s or 2s. The file then passed 8 of 8 runs.

AC3 IS OPEN: no reviewer pass has run yet. Not verified on a GitHub runner: that the runner decodes %25 in an annotation, and whether "Re-run failed jobs" reads a corrected variable.

POSSIBLE FOLLOW-UP, not filed from here because of file scope: this guard fires only after npm publish, so a malformed variable still puts a red X on a release that did publish. Checking the variable before the publish step, and in publish: false rehearsals as publish-release.sh does for --dry-run, would stop that. The runbook's LCLI-629 paragraph could also name release.yml as a fourth reader.

REVIEW FIXES, opum-ai/lore-cli#358, commit ba928815. The reviewer's verdict at 2edab0a3 was SHIP-WITH-NITS, relayed by the coordinator. Two items were addressed here; the coordinator is filing the other nits separately.

1. LOW, lone CR. The malformed list gains a\rb, expected to print as $'a\rb'. I checked that rendering on macOS /bin/bash 3.2.57 and in an ubuntu:24.04 container running bash 5.2.21. The one-line assertion now splits on CR as well as LF. The claim that the runner splits on CR is the reviewer's; I did not measure it.
   Mutant: keep %q, then turn its \r escape back into a raw CR with shown="${shown//\\r/$'\r'}". This leaves every other case unchanged.
   - New suite on the mutant: 18 pass, 1 fail. The only red is the a\rb case.
   - Pre-review suite (2edab0a3) on the same mutant: 18 of 18 pass. So the gap was real.
   - Unmutated fix: 19 of 19 pass.
2. NIT, variable scopes. The refusal now reads: "It comes from vars.REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS, which can be set as a release-environment, repository or organisation variable, the most specific one winning: correct it there, or delete it at every level for the 1800s default." The precedence is GitHub's documented order; I did not measure it.

GATES (local macOS; bun 1.3.14, lore 0.11.0 from source, shellcheck 0.11.0, actionlint 1.7.12):
- The new test file: 19 pass on 10 of 10 back-to-back runs, plus once more after the comment edit.
- bun test (full): exit 0. 4328 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail across 4329 tests in 121 files.
- bun run lint: exit 0. Its 4 warnings and 1 info are all in untouched files.
- bun run lint:shell: exit 0.
- actionlint release.yml: exit 0.
- bun run lore check: exit 0 (82 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings).

AC3 (reviewer pass) stays unchecked for the dispatcher. The review happened, but checking the box is the dispatcher's decision.
